baseline.label: Endogenous · unrestrained meal
baseline.note: With no drug on board the satiation signal accumulates slowly; a meal runs most of its course before the signal reaches the threshold that ends it.

stages.label: GLP-1RA
stages.note: The therapeutic peptide persists in blood for days — unlike native gut GLP-1, which is degraded within minutes. It is sensed wherever the blood-brain barrier is open.

stages.label: Gastric stretch
stages.note: Stretch receptors in the stomach wall report meal volume — a mechanical satiation signal carried by sensory vagal fibres.

stages.label: Gastric emptying
stages.note: GLP-1RAs slow the stomach, prolonging distension and blunting the post-meal glucose rise — a genuine peripheral contributor that partly habituates with chronic dosing.

stages.label: Vagal afferents
stages.note: Sensory vagal fibres carry gut mechanical and chemical signals to the nucleus tractus solitarius — an indirect, partial route, not the only one.

stages.label: Area postrema
stages.note: The area postrema lies outside the blood-brain barrier — the privileged interface where circulating drug is sensed directly. The NTS integrates that with vagal input.

stages.label: Arcuate nucleus
stages.note: Melanocortin balance shifts toward satiety: POMC neurons are activated, AgRP hunger-drive neurons suppressed.

stages.label: Paraventricular
stages.note: The PVN integrates arcuate and brainstem input into a coordinated meal-termination output.

stages.label: Meal terminates
stages.note: The meal ends earlier and smaller; ad libitum energy intake and subjective hunger both fall — the directly measurable endpoint.

edges.note: sensed directly at the BBB-free area postrema
slowed emptying sustains the stretch signal

regimes.label: Liraglutide · daily therapeutic
regimes.prose: Daily liraglutide reduces intake partly through the periphery you can measure: it slows gastric emptying and raises satiation, so the meal ends sooner. The gastric-emptying effect is largest early and partly habituates — the arcuate and brainstem signalling carry more of the sustained effect.

regimes.label: Semaglutide · weekly therapeutic
regimes.prose: Weekly semaglutide drives the satiation signal steeper still: ad libitum energy intake falls by roughly a quarter and hunger ratings drop. The margin to the aversion threshold narrows — nausea is the dose-limiting side effect, and on this curve it is the same accumulating signal reaching the malaise line near a full meal's worth of intake.

regimes.label: Exendin-4 · experimental · acute
regimes.prose: Acute high-dose experimental dosing in rodents drives the signal so steeply that the curve crosses the aversion threshold well within a single meal. This is the regime in which conditioned taste aversion and pica are reliably produced — a reminder that 'suppresses intake' and 'produces malaise' are the same curve read at two heights, not two separate findings.

gaps.label: The cascade is drawn as tonic
gaps.note: A static cascade implies a steady satiety dial. The brain's own GLP-1 signal is phasic — recruited in bursts by large meals and stress, near-silent otherwise. A drug holds that transient signal on continuously.

gaps.label: It says nothing about wanting
gaps.note: Homeostatic satiety does not explain reduced cue-driven craving, lower progressive-ratio breakpoints, or why the effect generalises to alcohol and nicotine. That is a mesolimbic incentive-salience story the cascade has no node for.

gaps.label: It cannot tell satiety from malaise
gaps.note: The cascade ends at a single node — 'meal terminates'. The curve shows there are two thresholds, not one: the same signal that ends a meal, pushed further, is nausea and visceral aversion.

openQuestions: How much of chronic GLP-1RA intake suppression is peripheral (gastric emptying, satiation) versus central (arcuate, brainstem) once gastric-emptying tachyphylaxis is accounted for?
Is the aversion threshold a fixed property of the circuitry, or does it recalibrate under chronic dosing — and would that explain why nausea typically wanes while appetite suppression persists?
Does the melanocortin (POMC / AgRP) account add anything the brainstem satiation circuitry does not, or is the arcuate's role largely permissive?
